- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +2–4% above peak.
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–2% downward buffer to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–3 day delay in price correction.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often overreacts to recent events; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per event.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to forecast path (e.g., 3-day moving average).
